statement: A page may have an implied grid that elements align to even when the grid itself is invisible.
Related elements should share meaningful horizontal and vertical alignment seams across adjacent surfaces, even when their containers differ.
Components must respect the geometry of the spatial system they render inside: parent bounds, padding, sibling seams, alignment lines, and anchor geometry.
A sidebar editorial card should normally occupy the sidebar content width minus canonical padding.
A layout should have a small number of alignment lines; each new seam must earn its place.
Edge alignment beats center alignment for text-heavy and tool-dense layouts.
Elements sharing a common edge read as related; a seam broken without intent reads as accidental.
Baseline alignment should hold across adjacent columns and siblings of text.
Optical alignment overrides mathematical alignment for shapes that read as off-center when geometrically centered.
Nested containers inherit alignment intent from their parent rather than re-centering independently.

sources.title: Mature design systems (Atlassian, Material, Carbon, Fluent, Polaris)

statement: Adjacent regions with similar content should share column geometry and gutter rhythm where widths allow.

sources.title: Mature design systems (Atlassian, Material, Carbon, Fluent, Polaris)

statement: Interior negative space should be balanced so centered content does not appear to drift.
An element that intentionally breaks the grid must break it decisively; near-misses read as bugs.
Spacing values come from the canonical spacing scale; one-off pixel values are suspect.
Spacing within a group is tighter than spacing between groups, so proximity encodes relatedness.
Visual rhythm comes from repeating consistent intervals, not from equal distribution of content.
Optical padding compensation is acceptable where shape geometry makes uniform padding look uneven.
Density is chosen per surface: tools may be dense; marketing and reading surfaces stay breathable.

sources.title: Mature design systems (Atlassian, Material, Carbon, Fluent, Polaris)

statement: Increase whitespace before adding separators or chrome.
Interactive target minimums hold regardless of how tight the visual spacing becomes.
Vertical spacing between repeated items is identical so lists read as one rhythm.
Compact density never justifies clipped or unreadable text.
Trailing space at the end of scrollable regions is deliberate, not residual layout accident.

sources.title: Mature design systems (Atlassian, Material, Carbon, Fluent, Polaris)

statement: Consistent spacing asymmetry (e.g., more space below a heading than above) encodes grouping direction.
Each view has one primary action; competing primary actions are a hierarchy failure.
Every screen has a single dominant focal element; when two elements compete, the hierarchy has failed.
Progressive disclosure shows essentials first and reveals complexity only on demand.
Heading levels reflect true document hierarchy, not visual convenience.
Essential content and actions must not depend on hover to be discovered.
Visual weight tracks importance; decorative elements remain subordinate.
Compelling hierarchy invites scroll; critical content is not crammed above a fold line.
Destructive actions are visually separated from and never styled like primary actions.

sources.title: Mature design systems (Atlassian, Material, Carbon, Fluent, Polaris)

statement: Key information sits on natural scan paths; users scan, they do not read every word.
Empty states teach the next action rather than only announcing absence of data.

sources.title: Mature design systems (Atlassian, Material, Carbon, Fluent, Polaris)

statement: Recommended options may be visually emphasized to reduce decision cost.
Body text keeps a measure of roughly 45-75 characters per line.
Line height scales with measure: longer lines need more leading.
Font sizes come from a modular type scale; arbitrary sizes are suspect.

sources.title: Mature design systems (Atlassian, Material, Carbon, Fluent, Polaris)

statement: Display and heading sizes are set tighter than body text.
Lowercase body text is never letterspaced; tracking adjustments belong to caps and display type.
All-caps is reserved for short labels and gets added letterspacing.
Product source uses the canonical typefaces only; other faces require an approved exception.
Orphaned words in display lines are resolved on editorial surfaces where feasible.
Tabular figures are used for numeric columns so digits align.
Hierarchy is built from size, weight, and spacing within one family before adding fonts.
Justified text requires hyphenation control; otherwise use ragged-right.
Body text meets canonical minimum sizes for the surface (roughly 16px equivalent on web).
Punctuation that hangs outside the measure (hanging punctuation) improves flush edges in display settings.
Accent color communicates semantic state or a named data category, never decoration.
One canonical accent hue anchors the palette; multi-accent rainbow treatments require explicit intent.
Semantic colors keep identical meaning across every surface.

sources.title: Mature design systems (Atlassian, Material, Carbon, Fluent, Polaris)

statement: Color alone never carries the only signal for meaning or state.
Text meets contrast minimums (4.5:1 normal, 3:1 large) against its rendered background.
Generated gradients anchor on the canonical accent as dominant hue and stay subordinate to content.
On dark surfaces, elevation is expressed by lightness steps rather than shadow alone.

sources.title: Mature design systems (Atlassian, Material, Carbon, Fluent, Polaris)

statement: Imagery incompatible with the color system is rejected or deliberately color-graded to harmonize.
The strongest chroma is reserved for the smallest, most important elements.
The neutral palette carries the interface; saturation is spent deliberately and sparingly.
Focus and selection states remain distinguishable without relying on hue shift alone.
Album art, merch shots, and faces are never cropped or covered with chrome; art is sacred content.
Backgrounds are abstract light, atmosphere, or restrained texture — never literal focal objects competing with content.
Hero imagery is composed for its final layout: it reserves headline, subcopy, and control zones, with depth falling off optically from the focal plane.
Background media is content-aware: compositionally safe regions are generated for text instead of masking poor composition with opaque overlays.
Faces and subjects in imagery frame or lead toward the content, not away from it.
Crops preserve subject intent; avoid amputating joints, heads, or meaningful detail.
Image treatments (grade, duotone, crop language) stay consistent within a surface family.

sources.title: Mature design systems (Atlassian, Material, Carbon, Fluent, Polaris)

statement: Decorative imagery never pushes overlaid text below contrast minimums.
Opaque readability rectangles behind text are an anti-pattern when content-aware generation can solve the composition.
Product screenshots in marketing show real product UI at readable scale.
Illustration and generated media stay within one consistent style family per surface.

sources.title: Mature design systems (Atlassian, Material, Carbon, Fluent, Polaris)

statement: Depth cues — elevation, shadow, border — encode real layering, never decoration.

sources.title: Mature design systems (Atlassian, Material, Carbon, Fluent, Polaris)

statement: Rounded artwork sitting on a visible square backing plate is an anti-pattern.
Corner radius comes from a scale; sibling surfaces share radius language.

sources.title: Mature design systems (Atlassian, Material, Carbon, Fluent, Polaris)

statement: Between hairline borders and fill contrast, choose the quieter separation first.
Elevation uses few levels; arbitrary z-axis variety reads as noise.

sources.title: Mature design systems (Atlassian, Material, Carbon, Fluent, Polaris)

statement: Glass and translucency must preserve legibility of content both beneath and above the material.
Interactive surfaces signal interactivity; static surfaces never borrow interactive chrome.
Dividers are the last resort after spacing and grouping fail to separate content.

sources.title: Mature design systems (Atlassian, Material, Carbon, Fluent, Polaris)

statement: A sidebar-triggered dropdown normally stays within the sidebar width unless content legibility or accessibility requires escape.
An overlay anchored inside a container respects that container's geometry; escaping requires a deliberate reason.
The user's current location is always evident in navigation.
Menus and popovers open adjacent to their trigger and dismiss predictably.
Primary navigation stays within a small count; overflow moves to secondary patterns.
Overlays never obscure the content they annotate.
Every pushed view, sheet, or modal has an obvious way back.
Persistent chrome stays quieter than the content it frames.
Popover positioning flips to stay visible before it clips.

sources.title: Mature design systems (Atlassian, Material, Carbon, Fluent, Polaris)

statement: Every interactive component defines hover, focus, active, disabled, and loading states.

sources.title: Mature design systems (Atlassian, Material, Carbon, Fluent, Polaris)

statement: Empty, loading, error, and success states are designed states, not framework defaults.

sources.title: Mature design systems (Atlassian, Material, Carbon, Fluent, Polaris)

statement: Error messages say what happened and what to do next in plain language.
Form fields carry visible labels; placeholder text is never the label.
Tables align numeric columns with tabular figures and right alignment; text columns align left.
Cards group related content; cards nested inside cards are suspect.

sources.title: Mature design systems (Atlassian, Material, Carbon, Fluent, Polaris)

statement: Irreversible actions get explicit confirmation friction proportional to the cost of error.
Content regions prefer skeletons shaped like the real layout over generic spinners.

sources.title: Mature design systems (Atlassian, Material, Carbon, Fluent, Polaris)

statement: A disabled control explains or hints at why it is disabled when the reason is ambiguous.
One canonical component family owns a concept; supported states are variants consumed as instances.
Layouts adapt composition to the viewport rather than scaling everything down uniformly.

sources.title: Mature design systems (Atlassian, Material, Carbon, Fluent, Polaris)

statement: Touch targets stay at least 44 points on touch surfaces regardless of density.
Breakpoints follow content needs, not a device catalog.

sources.title: Mature design systems (Atlassian, Material, Carbon, Fluent, Polaris)

statement: Multi-column layouts collapse in content-priority order, not mechanically left-to-right.

sources.title: Mature design systems (Atlassian, Material, Carbon, Fluent, Polaris)

statement: Horizontal scrolling of primary content on mobile is a failure.
Reading measure is preserved across breakpoints by re-wrapping, not overflow.
Hover-dependent affordances need an equivalent touch path.
Seam alignment rules are per-context: seams aligned on desktop may intentionally release on stacked mobile.

sources.title: Mature design systems (Atlassian, Material, Carbon, Fluent, Polaris)

statement: Motion communicates spatial continuity: where elements came from and where they went.
Interface motion feels instant, roughly 100-300ms; longer durations must earn their time.

sources.title: Mature design systems (Atlassian, Material, Carbon, Fluent, Polaris)

statement: Animations are interruptible and reversible without visible jumps.
Experiences honor reduced-motion preferences with non-animated equivalents.
Easing follows physical intuition: decelerate on entry, accelerate on exit.

sources.title: Mature design systems (Atlassian, Material, Carbon, Fluent, Polaris)

statement: Staggered reveals order attention; gratuitous staggering is noise.

sources.title: Mature design systems (Atlassian, Material, Carbon, Fluent, Polaris)

statement: Motion never blocks interaction; controls respond before animation completes.
Layout-shifting motion is used only when it explains a state change.

sources.title: Mature design systems (Atlassian, Material, Carbon, Fluent, Polaris)

statement: Shared-element continuity beats crossfades for navigational transitions.
Decorative icons and emoji carry no border, ring, circle, or badge plate.
Icons within a set share stroke weight, grid, and optical size.

sources.title: Mature design systems (Atlassian, Material, Carbon, Fluent, Polaris)

statement: Icons carry labels when their meaning is not universal; critical actions never rely on icon alone.
Generated media meets the same quality bar as hand-crafted assets.
Approved reusable cast, wardrobe, and asset references are preferred over unconstrained generation when they improve taste consistency.
Logos normalize visible ink through the shared asset registry, never route-local crop or scale CSS.
Emoji are not a substitute for iconography in product UI.
Media aspect ratio is owned by the layout, not by whatever the asset shipped with.
Designs are validated against real content; truncation and overflow strategy is part of the design.

sources.title: Mature design systems (Atlassian, Material, Carbon, Fluent, Polaris)

statement: Long content wraps or truncates deliberately, always with an affordance to access the rest.
Empty space is a tool; crowding a layout to fill space is a smell.
Content dictates layout; content is never distorted to satisfy a grid.
Dates, numbers, and statuses format consistently across surfaces.

sources.title: Mature design systems (Atlassian, Material, Carbon, Fluent, Polaris)

statement: Sparse first-run states still look intentionally designed.

sources.title: Mature design systems (Atlassian, Material, Carbon, Fluent, Polaris)

statement: Labels fit their controls across supported text lengths and locales.
A hero pairs one sharp claim with a single primary CTA and product truth.
Every product page demonstrates the real product UI; no section ships as unstyled text.
Social proof stays visually subordinate to the message it supports.
Sections alternate rhythm between dense and airy to sustain attention down the page.
Callouts and annotations never overlap product UI unintentionally.
One hero per story; multiple competing focal areas dilute the narrative.
Calls to action repeat down the page with increasing commitment.
Product media frames the product truthfully; no fake chrome or misleading stagecraft.
The opening section answers what the product is, who it is for, and why it matters within seconds.
Pricing and FAQ sections reduce risk through plain, scannable structure.
Founder review surfaces contain canonical masters and intentional variants only — no receipts, duplicates, or filler.
All functionality is reachable by keyboard with a visible focus indicator.
Content remains usable zoomed to 200% and reflowed at narrow viewports.
Alt text conveys the function of imagery, not a description of its pixels.
Form errors are identified in text and programmatically associated with their fields.
Heading and landmark structure is navigable by screen readers.
Focus is never trapped, and it returns to a sensible place when overlays close.
Autoplaying media with sound is prohibited; moving content needs pause controls.
Controls expose accessible names matching their visible labels.
Status messages announced to assistive tech do not rely on receiving focus.
Dragging-only interactions have single-pointer alternatives.
Craft signals matter: clean seams, aligned edges, no orphaned one-off overrides.
Premium feel comes from restraint: fewer elements, better spacing, calibrated type.
Every visible element answers why it is there; anything without an answer is removed.
Consistency across surfaces is itself a quality signal.
Perceived responsiveness is a design quality, not only an engineering metric.
Interface copy is edited, terse, and human; copy quality is design quality.
Default and zero-data states look finished, never like placeholders.

sources.title: Mature design systems (Atlassian, Material, Carbon, Fluent, Polaris)

statement: Fit-and-finish bugs — clipping, overflow, jank — erode trust disproportionate to their size.
When in doubt, remove: each element must justify its existence.
Prefer whitespace over dividers, dividers over boxes, boxes over chrome.
Gradients, shadows, and borders compound; a surface rarely needs more than one.
Defaults are quiet; emphasis is spent where it matters.
Decoration that serves neither hierarchy nor meaning is removed.
The best tooltip is clarity that makes the tooltip unnecessary.
Feature abundance must not surface as visual abundance.
Internal scaffolding and audit chrome never render in customer-facing UI.
Approved people and cast references are preferred for humans in generated media.
Approved wardrobe and clothing references keep human imagery taste-consistent.
Device frames and product mockups come from the canonical set.
Reusable visual assets carry named ids and provenance; generation does not re-derive them ad hoc.
Photographic treatment — grade, crop, depth — follows approved references rather than per-prompt improvisation.
Customer artwork (album art, avatars, covers) is treated as immutable sacred content.
Recognition beats recall: show options and state rather than requiring memory.
Users should always know what the system is doing through timely feedback.
Interfaces match the user's language and mental model, not system internals.
Consistency in patterns lets users transfer learned behavior across surfaces.
Prevent errors where possible; make recovery cheap where not.
Accelerators for expert users coexist with discoverability for novices.
Aesthetic-minimalist design removes irrelevant or rarely needed information from view.
Help and recovery content is findable at the moment of need.
The time to acquire a target grows with distance and shrinks with size; primary actions are large and near.
Cognitive load is reduced by chunking related information.
Elements close together are perceived as a group; spacing is a grouping signal.
Elements sharing enclosed regions are perceived as related; use enclosures sparingly.
Similar appearance implies similar function; visually distinct elements should behave differently.
Elements on shared connected paths read as one flow; break continuity only to signal a break.
Symmetrical elements read as belonging together; asymmetry signals a distinction.
The eye completes incomplete shapes; favor closure and figure-ground clarity over literal rendering.
Navigation depth trades against breadth: few clicks matter less than clear wayfinding.
Serial position matters: first and last items in a list are remembered best.
Choices expand the time to decide; constrain option sets presented at once.
Peak-end: the most intense moment and the ending shape remembered experience; design both.
Reusable page regions derive from shared section templates rather than bespoke rebuilds.
Scroll-hijacking and fake scroll experiences are an anti-pattern on content pages.
Fixed elements shrink the usable canvas; persistent chrome must earn its footprint.
Animation that loops indefinitely must be ambient, slow, and ignorable.

sources.title: Mature design systems (Atlassian, Material, Carbon, Fluent, Polaris)

statement: Text Button size names share one equivalent visible control inside a minimum hit target.
Marketing logo marks render at canonical size and align with neighboring controls.
Avatar imagery centers the face and preserves it at small sizes.

sources.title: Mature design systems (Atlassian, Material, Carbon, Fluent, Polaris)

statement: A design review queue never asks a human to re-decide an unchanged decision.
Unknown future content gets safe generic treatment instead of a bespoke guess.

sources.title: Mature design systems (Atlassian, Material, Carbon, Fluent, Polaris)

statement: User control and freedom: undo beats confirm where the action is reversible.
Consistency between marketing and product surfaces protects brand trust.
Error-prone conditions are designed out, not messaged around.
Placeholder and skeleton content uses realistic proportions, not gray boxes.

sources.title: Mature design systems (Atlassian, Material, Carbon, Fluent, Polaris)

statement: Touch and pointer interactions provide immediate visual feedback on contact.
Scrollable regions signal their scrollability with affordance, not hidden overflow.
Icon-only toolbars pair with tooltips or labels for discoverability.
